title: I Took the Didgeridoo Checkout to the Lead Who Skipped the Beeswax Log

parts.text: I stepped into the drone room at 4:08 p.m. and lead Tamsin was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE PIPE. FORTY-FIVE MINUTES. WAX STAYS WITH THE CHECKOUT. I was twenty-six, studio secretary, holding a checkout that listed our numbered wax. Tamsin shrugged. "Leads are the drone." I photographed the board, the booking, and her leftover mouthpiece on my numbered wax. Then I asked for the wax log. At 4:16 the desk pinged why Tamsin's name was on my beeswax. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The desk can see Tamsin's leftover mouthpiece on my numbered wax.

social.video_title: She skipped the beeswax log on my didgeridoo checkout — Part 1/2
social.description: Drone room, leftover mouthpiece, a forty-five-minute clock she posted. I logged the wax. Would you have asked for the wax log?

parts.text: Tamsin called it circular practice until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the mouthpiece still. The wax went back to my numbered checkout. Tamsin ran a slot of her own and told the next lead atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: LEADS ARE NOT THE DRONE. I keep my wax in a labeled tin. Tamsin brown-bags her circles. The drone room finally looks like a checkout, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Leads are not the drone — Part 2/2
social.description: Wax log, numbered beeswax, and a second line on the board. Was circular practice ever my mouthpiece?
